harness: 0bfe1e06f22400aa89db33e471007b1036c3b79d (private harness; the attempt-14 harness unchanged, run as listed under harnessChanges)
host: the private acceptance host (AMD Ryzen 5 3600, 12 cpu, 64 GiB, NVMe RAID1/ext4, Ubuntu 24.04, Linux 6.8.0-139-generic); one emulator at a time; official emulator on untuned HotSpot defaults (JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS empty, heap up to a quarter of RAM) with Java 26.0.2.1 and firebase-tools 15.22.0; the Firenook stack ran without Java and without firebase-tools; Node 24.20.0

pairedAcceptance.result: PASS (result.passed, controller/smoke/full exit 0; 95 evidence checksums re-verified by an independent audit that re-derives every percentile and memory peak from the raw samples and asserts the candidate, binary, seed and consumer pins)
pairedAcceptance.workload: sequential official then Firenook: cheap smoke, 7,200 s app-shaped soak (two busy sessions plus an idle observer), export/restart, nine browser journeys before and after restart, then a fresh checkout on the default backend and on the documented official fallback; the attempt-14 workload unchanged
pairedAcceptance.stableStateParity: 1 Auth user, 211,205 Firestore documents and 33,352 stable Storage objects (6,688,940,031 bytes) on both stacks after every soak, journey set and restart
pairedAcceptance.soakCounts: both soaks exact: 480 catalogue reads, 240 function dispatches, 1,440 gateway writes, 960 status writes, 2,880 token batches (57,600 token writes), 240 Storage cycles, observer 240 + 120; 0 errors, 0 stalls, 0 acknowledged-state mismatches, 0 duplicate effects

peakEmulatorPssGiB.process: the emulator by name: java (official) and firenook; the consumer's web server is the largest process of the Firenook stack, so the top process is not the emulator

consumerWebServerPssGiB.note: the same on both stacks; 7.4 GiB in the attempt-14 run, at an earlier consumer revision

memory.swap: swap emptied before each stack started; the official stack then held 7.7 GB of swap at the start of its soak and paged out 765,740 more pages during it; the Firenook stack held 1.6 GB and paged out 0

hostBytesWrittenDuringSoak.note: whole host; the official emulator keeps its data in memory until it exports, Firenook makes every acknowledged write durable within a second

initialReadiness.note: application readiness including the consumer's own builds and probes; both stacks import the seed

restartReadiness.note: both stacks import the export taken after the soak

lastEmulatorPortOpen.note: initial / restart; Firenook binds every listener once ready, after the import and its ordered index; the consumer's web server compiles at the same time

pairedAcceptance.browserJourneys: 36/36 passes (nine journeys, both stacks, before and after restart), 0 page errors, 0 request failures; the catalogue journey still ends on the watcher's heartbeat on Firenook (89.6 / 97.2 s against 31.5 / 31.6 official) because the frozen runner's synthetic stimulus lacks the observer's filter field: the official emulator notifies a listener for a document its filter excludes, Firenook does not (recorded since the next.4 qualification; not an emulator latency)
pairedAcceptance.regressions: 11/11 harness, engine (cargo fmt, clippy --all-features --all-targets, cargo test), packaging and consumer build commands exit 0
pairedAcceptance.comparedWithAttempt14: official medians agree within noise (write 202.8 -> 208.2 ms, listener 203 -> 209 ms). Firenook (0.2.0-next.6 -> 0.2.0): write p50 5.3 -> 5.1 ms, listener p50 11 -> 11 ms, catalogue read p50 6.9 -> 6.6 ms, emulator peak 2.16 -> 2.11 GiB

harnessChanges.unchangedFromAttempt14: the harness revision, contract, workload, seed and runner of the 0.2.0-next.6 run (attempt 14); the consumer application moved to a later revision, the same on both stacks
harnessChanges.emptyBuildCache: every stack starts the consumer's web server with an empty build cache before the smoke and again before the full run, after attempt 15 failed on a stale cache (the official stack's login page answered 404)
harnessChanges.hostDisk: attempt 16 passed both soaks and restarts, then the fresh-checkout preflight found 66.9 GB free against the manifest's 80 GB minimum; the host was given room and the run repeated unchanged as attempt 17
harnessChanges.stopSignal: the harness stops Firenook with SIGINT to the engine, so the launcher reports an unexpected exit (code 1) after a clean stop; the data closes cleanly and the next start needs no repair (follow-up below)

standalone.scope: after the paired run, on the same host: Firestore, Auth and Storage only, the same seed, no consumer application, one emulator at a time

upgradeFromNext8.note: the first start builds the ordered index once (7.4 s of the 8.0 s); 0.2.0-next.8 opens a store 0.2.0 wrote and builds its own index again

queryShapes.runs: 26 shapes, one warm-up and 25 timed runs each, over gRPC against Firestore holding the seed; three rounds on 0.2.0 (median shown), one on the official emulator and one on 0.2.0-next.8
queryShapes.identicalAnswers: 28/28 (each shape's documents in the same order with the same data, plus four walks over a whole collection that the ordered index serves)
queryShapes.note: the tie reads 500 document ids with no fields; each document is read whole before its fields are dropped

grownStore.officialDefaults: ready in 50.34 s at 14.98 GiB, then out of memory loading the data at the first query, which failed after 3 minutes

writeAB.rounds: next.8, 0.2.0, next.8, 0.2.0, each on a fresh copy of the seeded store: 2,000 sequential writes each confirmed by a listener, then 4,000 writes from eight concurrent writers
writeAB.result: keeping the ordered index did not slow writes

followUps: a clean engine exit (code 0) without a launcher signal is reported as unexpected; the launcher should treat it as a stop
select() with no fields still reads each document whole (the one query shape that ties)
evidence: private acceptance report, attempt 17 (audit summary, per-lane timelines, 95 checksummed evidence files) and the standalone results (lifecycle, upgrade, query shapes and answers, grown store, write A/B)
